title: Purpose and result in context
subtitle: Keep intended aim distinct from stated outcome.
overview: ἵνα commonly introduces purpose or intended outcome; ὥστε introduces a result. Their meanings depend on how they attach to the preceding clause.
Map the main action first, then ask whether the following clause gives its aim or its consequence.

sections.title: Aim or result?
rows: with the result that they were amazed
he gave ... so that they may have life

items.grc: ταῦτα γέγραπται ἵνα πιστεύσητε ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός.
items.en: These things have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ.

items.grc: ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον ὥστε συνάγεσθαι πρὸς αὐτὸν πολλούς.
items.en: He was speaking the word to them, with the result that many gathered to him.
